OMG, you have to read this and if you're a reporter, you really need to write this up. Absolutely wild. @BaniasLaw handles this with his usual professionalism, but the public needs to get an inside look at how agencies work on the inside.


Banias Law (@BaniasLaw)

#USCIS Adjudicators Gone Wild: 

If you've ever wondered what @USCIS adjudicators at your local Field Office talk about, here is a little insight. I got text messages between two @USCIS adjudicators who happen to be married. 

Some Co

A woman who experienced a miscarriage in detention received no medical care for 10 days, was deported in an acute medical crisis, and had her life saved only because reception center workers in Honduras rushed her to an emergency room. 

austinkocher.substack.com/p/…

Video

Using airport access as a political weapon sets a dangerous precedent. Federal infrastructure exists to serve the public, not as bargaining chip for political agendas.

The full story: notus.org/trump-white-house/…

Substack: austinkocher.substack.com

Mullin also claimed "just shy of 3 million" people have been deported or self-deported since January 2025. That number has not been independently verified and far exceeds official removal figures that have been made public. Mullin isn't diff from Noem, he's just more of the same.

Mullin framed this explicitly as retaliation. His words: "We need to focus on cities that want to work with us." That framing treats basic public infrastructure as a political reward, following in the footsteps of the basic cronyism that the Trump admin is notorious for.

The cities named as targets (New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Philadelphia, and San Francisco) are home to some of the busiest international airports in the United States. Pulling officers from those hubs would affect millions of travelers, not just immigrants.

CBP officers process people arriving on an international flights. Without them, airports would not be able to accept international travelers. The move (questionable legality) wouldn't affect undoc immigrants but would create pandemonium for lawful travelers across the country.

New DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin is says he's considering pulling customs officers from airports in so called "sanctuary cities" in an effort to punish jurisdictions that don't want to play ball with Trump's mass deportation plans. 🧵

This is not an isolated case. Military families, DACA recipients, people with no criminal record are all inside the current enforcement perimeter. 
Read more at 

The Guardian:theguardian.com/us-news/2026…

Follow me: austinkocher.substack.com

When ICE agents arrived, Blank's parents said the agents "seemed apologetic" and told them: "The higher-ups made them do it." That detail matters. It reflects a policy choice, not a field judgment. Individual agents don't set enforcement priorities.

Ramos and Blank had already hired a lawyer and filed paperwork to begin the green card process through marriage. They were doing everything the legal system asks of people. Enforcement found them anyway, at an Army base visitor center.

She applied for DACA in 2020, but her application was never processed after Trump's first administration stopped accepting new applicants. That decision left hundreds of thousands in legal limbo, with no path forward and no protection.

Ramos has no criminal history. She is a biochemistry student who teaches Sunday school. Her deportation order dates to 2005 (when she was an infant) after her family missed a court hearing. She has lived in the U.S. her entire life.

Annie Ramos, 22, was detained by ICE last Thursday at a Louisiana military base, days after marrying U.S. Army Staff Sgt. Matthew Blank, who is preparing to deploy. This case tells us something important about who this enforcement is actually targeting. 🧵

Zain Lakhani explains how the United States is creating a long-term family separation crisis that will last for decades and why we urgently need to build an international family reunification system.

Link: austinkocher.substack.com/p/…

Video

Join me tomorrow at 1 PM Eastern for a discussion with Julie Moreno about what life is like now, months after her husband Neff left the country￼.
